messages:
maria: FYI — found a small but nasty onboarding bug in the quickstart sampleapp. If you enable the SDK retry middleware + streaming response, some server-side side-effects execute twice after a 429. repro steps attached.
kevin: repro? logs? which SDK and sample?
sam: saw that with node-sdk v0.9.1 in the sample that demonstrates streaming chat. basically client sends request with Idempotency-Key, we hit a quota spike -> 429 mid-stream, SDK retries whole request, server re-applies side-effect because the idempotency header got dropped in our sample middleware.
maria: exact symptoms: webhook triggered twice, DB write dup, user sees duplicate confirmation. Happened on fresh account during guided quickstart. Not widespread but reproducible.
kevin: ah ok. looks like our sampleapp middleware strips extra headers during the stream->retry path. streaming retry path falls back to a plain resend without preserving idempotency header.
sam: proposed quick mitigation: sampleapp should attach a clientempotency layer that generates a stable key per client action and persists it for the safe-replay window. also add jittered backoff to avoid synchronized retries. e.g. exponential backoff + full jitter:
```js
const backoff = (attempt) => Math.floor(Math.random() * Math.min(2000, 300 * 2 ** attempt));
```
and keep idempotency-key in a small LRU cache for ~60s.
julie: agree with mitigation but nuance: we should NOT auto-retry streaming endpoints by default. For non-streaming requests, idempotency-key + retry is fine. For streaming we need either resume tokens or explicit "safe_replay" opt-in.
maria: makes sense. users on quickstart should get safe defaults. I propose: (1) sampleapp: enable clientempotency by default for normal requests, (2) disable auto-retry for streaming and show a banner explaining how to opt into resume-based replay.
kevin: parity question — will node and python SDKs behave the same? we shouldn't introduce platform surprise for new users.
sam: plan: implement clientempotency middleware in both SDKs. Node will export middleware function, Python will expose a RequestHook with identical config options (cache_ttl, jitter_base, max_cap). we can keep default behavior consistent: auto-retry true for non-stream, false for stream.
julie: i'll open a tiny RFC/PR: add clientempotency middleware to quickstart, document streaming opt-in, and add an integration test that asserts single side-effect on 429+retry. also add a short note in the SDK changelog about token-rotation race cases.
maria: thanks — can we also add a small README note for onboarding engineers: why idempotency matters and how to avoid unsafe replays (one-paragraph). new users hit this and it's a poor first impression. :point_up:
deploy-bot: deploy queued: docs-site/staging -> will publish after PR merge.
kevin: created a minimal repro gist and commented on the PR. will help QA.
sam: leaving a checklist in the PR: add LRU cache, backoff params, disable streaming auto-retry, doc blurb, e2e test.
julie: assigning to sam + kevin, target patch release in this sprint. thanks all :tada:
